payload.title: What Are the Samoan Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
protect_keywords: 5 samoan wedding traditions (old URL; SEO to quantify US and AU)
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian or New Zealand couple in their 30s with a generous budget, often with a Samoan partner or parents in the diaspora, who want to understand what the families will expect (speeches, fine mats, church, feast, taualuga), how to honour fa'a Samoa respectfully, and whether to marry in Samoa (Smartraveller: exercise normal safety precautions) or bring the customs into a wedding at home.
payload.goal: Read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine (primary CTA); secondary, in-context invitation to speak with a Wedded Advisor placed after the 'for Australians' section.
payload.angle: Most lists treat a Samoan wedding as a party with big numbers. We explain it as fa'a Samoa does: a meeting of two families, led by matai and orators, sealed in church and honoured with fine mats, a shared feast and the taualuga. Customs come in wedding order and in a confident, respectful voice, with meanings stated only where Te Papa, Auckland Museum, Britannica, UNESCO or Samoan government sources state them. We close with what Australians need to marry in Samoa, as Smartraveller and the Australian High Commission in Apia word it, or to bring these customs home.
must_include: One early framing line: practice varies by family, village and diaspora community; written as living practice ('In many Samoan families...')

About 10 numbered sections in wedding order: fa'a Samoa and matai, families' meeting and tulafale, 'ie toga and gifts, church wedding, extended family and village, dress, siva and taualuga, feast and umu, UNESCO, for Australians
Samoan terms with diacritics exactly as sources give them; a short glossary or inline definitions
Fine mats and gifts described with no amounts or counts
UNESCO 'ie Samoa element quoted only as far as its own text links to weddings, if confirmed live

Section for Australians: Smartraveller level and update date (as at November 2026), dengue and cyclone season, Sunday and village dress lines, same-sex recognition line stated neutrally once, 90 day Visitor Permit, Australian High Commission Apia for CNI and notarial, 'Getting married overseas', 'check with the registry and the high commission, including any fees'; Upolu and Savai'i only as places couples choose; Samoan-Australian weddings at home
FAQ of 5 to 7 questions with no amounts
Internal links: /destinations/oceania hub and a Fiji page as other Pacific destinations

tradition_plan.note: Planner (wedding-planner-sme) runs batch A and batch B in parallel, scratch folders 02-research/batch-a and 02-research/batch-b, 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, no extra sourcing rounds, never retry a declined call. Preferred sources: Te Papa (collections.tepapa.govt.nz), Auckland Museum (aucklandmuseum.com), Australian Museum (australian.museum), Britannica, Samoa Ministry of Education, Sports and Culture (mesc.gov.ws), samoa.travel, ich.unesco.org, academic sources. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs or Wikipedia. Unsourced customs are written as living practice with no meaning or origin as fact and no [[VERIFY]] marker; 'often told' at most once per post. Source gaps go in the run report only (authority rule).
